sources.title: On the Locus of Hodge Classes
sources.verified_scope: For a smooth projective family and a fixed cohomology class, the locus where the class remains of Hodge type is algebraic; used only to bind the Hodge-locus target, not to infer algebraicity of the class.

sources.title: Variational Hodge conjecture for complete intersections on hypersurfaces in projective space
sources.author: Remke Kloosterman
sources.verified_scope: Special-family positive calibration: a flag-Hilbert incidence can control a genuine varying hypersurface/Hodge locus for complete-intersection cycles. It is not transferred to arbitrary rational Hodge classes.

sources.title: Properties of the Hilbert functor, Lemma 108.7.7
sources.verified_scope: For a proper finite-presentation morphism with a chosen Hilbert polynomial, the Hilbert space is proper over the base.

sources.title: The Hilbert functor
sources.verified_scope: The relative Hilbert functor parametrizes closed subschemes flat over the parameter base; used for the universal flat witness families.

sources.title: Proper morphisms: base change
sources.verified_scope: Properness is preserved by base change; used when restricting the Hilbert product to the chosen Hodge branch.

sources.title: Smooth morphisms are universally open
sources.verified_scope: Reused only through merged C007's sufficient image certificate: smoothness at a source point supplies a nonempty open image.

technical_boundary.flat_family_cycle_class_constancy: Used as the standard topological fact that the fibre fundamental class of a flat proper family of algebraic cycles is locally constant in the pulled-back integral cohomology local system. In the frozen local contract the base U is contractible, so equality at the central witness propagates on its connected Hilbert component.
technical_boundary.pdf_visual_verification: NOT_APPLICABLE: no PDF was used as the technical evidence surface in this cycle; primary arXiv abstract/HTML and Stacks HTML were used.

negative_history: C006: full nonlinear image does not force selected-point differential surjectivity (ramification).
C007: selected-point tangent surjectivity does not force image coverage at a singular incidence source (cusp).
H4d1a: same-detector first-order kernel-free nonzero obstruction envelope is impossible.
strict_nonclaims: no smoothness or dominance of the constructed Hilbert incidence
no initial algebraicity for an arbitrary Hodge class
no higher-Artin lifting, algebraization/globalization, or monodromy closure
